chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samal has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Fudalah, from Al-'Uthaym, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samal.

key_terms.أَبُو بَكْرٍ بْنِ أَبِي صِمَالٍ: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samal, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.الْعَثِيمُ: Al-'Uthaym, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْفُضَيْلَةُ: Al-Fudalah, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific for companions or narrators
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a key transmitter in the chain

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain for narrations from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samal in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides this specific isnad to authenticate the reliability of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samal, a key narrator in the Kufan school, by tracing the chain back to the prominent scholar Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan al-Saffar. This clarification underscores the rigorous standards of hadith verification in Shia scholarship, ensuring that narrations attributed to this companion are grounded in a continuous and trustworthy lineage of transmission.
